name: A Sydney backyard

place_source.title: Wikidata: Sydney (Q3130), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban backyard in Sydney: a lawn, a border of bottlebrush and lilli pilli, a tall gum tree and a fig, visited by ibises, magpies, lorikeets and possums by day and by flying-foxes and tree frogs after dark.

facts.text: Sydney has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa) with warm summers and mild winters.

source.title: Wikipedia: Sydney
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Sydney", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Australian white ibis has become a common sight in Sydney's parks and shopping centre carparks since moving into urban areas in the 1970s.

source.title: Wikipedia: Australian white ibis
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Australian white ibis", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The grey-headed flying-fox is listed as vulnerable under federal law; Sydney's botanic gardens host one of the largest urban roosts.

source.title: Wikipedia: Grey-headed flying fox
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Grey-headed flying fox", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The common brushtail possum is one of the Australian marsupials most often seen by city dwellers, denning in tree hollows and house roofs.

source.title: Wikipedia: Common brushtail possum
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Common brushtail possum", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Australian magpie's carolling song is one of the most recognisable bird calls in Australia; males swoop to defend their nests in spring.

source.title: Wikipedia: Australian magpie
